speaker: Pilot
en: Flying over Pakistan, altitude 30,000 feet. Approaching Soviet airspace.

speaker: Pilot
en: Twenty minutes to dropoff... Commencing internal depressurization.

speaker: Pilot
en: Equipment check... arm main parachute.

speaker: Zero
en: All right. You ready to go?

speaker: Pilot
en: Drop zone still showing a high pressure mass. CAVOK.

speaker: Zero
en: Good, we've got high visibility.

speaker: Pilot
en: Approaching release point... Ten minutes to dropoff.

speaker: Zero
en: Hey! Are you deaf? He said put out the cigar and put on your mask.

speaker: Pilot
en: Depressurization complete. Checking oxygen supply. Six minutes to dropoff. Opening rear hatch. Sunrise... External temperature minus 46 degrees Celsius. Two minutes to dropoff. Stand up.

speaker: Zero
en: You'll be falling at 130 miles per hour. Try not to get frostbite from the wind chill.

speaker: Pilot
en: One minute to dropoff. Move to the rear. Activate bailout bottle.

speaker: Zero
en: This is one for the history books; the world's first HALO jump.

speaker: Pilot
en: Ten seconds to dropoff. Standby... Status OK, all green. Prepare for dropoff... Countdown, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

speaker: Zero
en: Spread your wings and fly! God be with you!

speaker: Zero
en: Jack, I've got some important news. The head of the CIA has finally given us the green light for the Virtuous mission.

speaker: Jack
en: Virtual mission?

speaker: Zero
en: No, the Virtuous mission. The future of our FOX unit depends on it. If it succeeds, we'll be officially organized into a unit.

speaker: Jack
en: Virtuous mission? Sounds like some kind initiation ritual.

speaker: Zero
en: Don't get cocky. This isn't a training a op.

speaker: Jack
en: Right. So what exactly is this wonderful mission?

speaker: Zero
en: Well... About two years ago, a certain Soviet scientist requested asylum in the West through one of our moles. His name is Nikolai Stepanovich Sokolov. He's head of the OKB-754 Design Bureau, one of the Soviet's top-secret weapon research facilities, and the East's foremost expert on weapons development.

speaker: Jack
en: Sokolov... isn't he that famous rocket scientist?

speaker: Zero
en: The very same. On April 12, 1961, the Soviets achieved the first manned space flight in history.

speaker: Jack
en: The Earth was blue, but there was no God.

speaker: Zero
en: Well spoken. The rocket that carried Yuri Gagarin into orbit was the A1, known as the Vostok rocket. Sokolov is said to be the man most responsible for the multi-engine cluster used in that rocket. After Gagarin's flight, Sokolov left rocket development to become the head of the newly established Design Bureau.

speaker: Jack
en: From a lowly technician to the head of a Design Bureau, that's quite a success story. So why'd he want to defect?

speaker: Zero
en: It seems he'd become afraid of his own creations.

speaker: Jack
en: Afraid?

speaker: Zero
en: Call it a crisis of conscience.

speaker: Jack
en: And for that, he left his country and his family behind and went over the fence?

speaker: Zero
en: Not exactly. One of his conditions was that his family was also to be taken safely to the West. We used a mole to get the family out first and succeeded in sneaking Sokolov over the Berlin Wall shortly afterwards. I was the one who conducted the operation.

speaker: Jack
en: The security on the Eastern side was still full of holes back then. Then what?

speaker: Zero
en: We got Sokolov over in one piece but the whole ordeal had left him exhausted, and we checked him into a hospital in West Berlin. It took him two weeks and over 600 miles to get from the research facility in the Soviet Union to Berlin. He was in no condition to say anything coherent. And it was only a week later that we had something much bigger on our hands.

speaker: Jack
en: The Cuban Missile Crisis.

speaker: Zero
en: October 16, 1962. President Kennedy received word that the Soviets were in the process of deploying intermediate-range ballistic missiles in Cuba. The president demanded that the Soviets dismantle and remove the missiles. At the same time, he announced a naval blockade to prevent further missile shipments from reaching Cuba. But the Soviets didn't back down, instead placing their armed forces on secondary alert. Soviet transport ships carrying missiles continued on course toward Cuba. US and Soviet forces went on alert for an all-out nuclear war. Frantic negotiations were conducted through the UN's Emergency Security Council and unofficial channels to end the hair-trigger standoff. Finally, on October 28, the Soviet Union agreed to remove its missiles from Cuba. And so the world avoided a nuclear holocaust. But in order to get the Soviets to pull their missiles out, we had to make a deal.

speaker: Jack
en: You mean the one where the US agreed to remove its IRBMs from Turkey?

speaker: Zero
en: No. The Jupiter IRBMs deployed in Turkey were obsolete and we were going to get rid of them anyway. They had no strategic value whatsoever to either the US or the Russians. The Turkey deal was a ruse - a cover story that was fed to the other intelligence agencies around the world.

speaker: Jack
en: So what did the Russians really want?

speaker: Zero
en: Sokolov. They wanted us to return Sokolov.

speaker: Jack
en: You mean the Soviets pulled out of Cuba just to get their hands on Sokolov?

speaker: Zero
en: That's right.

speaker: Jack
en: What the hell was he working on?

speaker: Zero
en: At the time we had no idea. We were running out of time. It was either give up Sokolov or risk full-scale nuclear war. In the end, we had no choice. President Kennedy gave into Khrushchev's demand. The next day, I got Sokolov out of the hospital and handed him over to agents on the eastern side. Sokolov kept on screaming "Save me!" until he disappeared from my sight. Then, a month ago, we received some new information from one of our moles.

speaker: Jack
en: About Sokolov?

speaker: Zero
en: Yes. He was taken back to the research facility and forced to continue working on the weapon in question under KGB supervision. What's more, it's on the verge of completion.

speaker: Jack
en: So? What kind of weapon is it? Something to do with space rockets?

speaker: Zero
en: No, missiles.

speaker: Jack
en: Same technology.

speaker: Zero
en: I guess you're right. We don't know the details but it appears to be a new kind of nuclear device. For a year now the Soviets have been conducting frequent nuclear tests at Semipaiatinsk.

speaker: Jack
en: Something to do with the weapon I assume.

speaker: Zero
en: We're talking about a secret weapon so big that Khrushchev was ready to pull out of Cuba to get it back.

speaker: Jack
en: Is Sokolov still in the facility?

speaker: Zero
en: According to our intelligence, he's in Tselinoyarsk, a place in the mountains about 3 miles to the west that's known as the Virgin Cliffs.

speaker: Jack
en: The Virgin Cliffs. Nice name for a Virtuous mission.

speaker: Zero
en: They moved him there just recently.

speaker: Jack
en: Why?

speaker: Zero
en: Apparently they're conducting a field test of the weapon. But it's our best chance to get him back. This mission would never have been possible if he were still in the research facility. This is our last chance. Sokolov must have known that, too, when he contacted us.

speaker: Zero
en: Listen up, Jack. Your mission is to infiltrate Tselinoyarsk in the Soviet mountains, ensure the safety of Sokolov, and bring him back to the West. If we don't get Sokolov back before that weapon is complete, we'll be facing a major crisis. The clock is ticking.

speaker: Zero
en: Once we've confirmed the rescue of Sokolov, stand by at the recovery point. A recovery balloon will be dropped at that point. Helium will be pumped into the balloon to inflate it. The process takes about 20 minutes. Once it's complete, the gunship's arm will latch onto the balloon and pull it up.

speaker: Jack
en: The Fulton Surface-to-Air Recovery System. I'm familiar with the theory.

speaker: Zero
en: Take it easy, it has been combat-proven.

speaker: Jack
en: Do you think Sokolov's up to it?

speaker: Zero
en: The shock will be less than during a parachute jump. And the arm can handle up to 500 pounds.

speaker: Jack
en: So you're planning to go over the border in a single Combat Talon?

speaker: Zero
en: She's equipped with two 6-barrel 20 millimeter Vulcan cannons as well as two 40 millimeter machine guns.

speaker: Jack
en: Sounds like she could hold her own against a battalion of tanks.

speaker: Zero
en: Even with the fuel in the reserve tank, we're facing a 4-hour time limit. If all goes well, it shouldn't take more than a few hours.

speaker: Jack
en: Home in time for dinner.

speaker: Zero
en: But if anything goes wrong, you'll be eating dinner, breakfast, and all the rest of your meals in the jungle.

speaker: Zero
en: Do you copy? You're already in enemy territory, and somebody might be listening in. From here on out, we'll be using codenames to refer to each other. Your codename for this mission will be Naked Snake. I'll be referring to you as Snake from now on. You are not to mention your real name.

speaker: Snake
en: "Snake"?

speaker: Zero
en: You don't like snakes?

speaker: Snake
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Zero
en: You've eaten on before, haven't you?

speaker: Snake
en: In survival training.

speaker: Zero
en: I'm glad to hear that.

speaker: Snake
en: I don't know if I'd ever order one in a restaurant, but...

speaker: Zero
en: Be careful, you might not have a choice.

speaker: Snake
en: What about you, Major? What should I call you?

speaker: Zero
en: Hmm, let's see... I'll be... I'll be Tom. Call me Major Tom.

speaker: Tom
en: Oh, and Snake...

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah?

speaker: Tom
en: The crew isn't watching anymore. You can take off the disguise now.

speaker: Snake
en: Good idea. This isn't right. Time for the snake to shed his skin.

speaker: Snake
en: Can you hear me, Major Tom? This is Snake. Kept you waiting, huh?

speaker: Tom
en: This will be a sneaking mission. You must not be seen by the enemy. You must leave no trace of your presence. Is that clear? This kind of infiltration is the FOX unit's specialty. In other words, weapons and equipment are procure on-site... that goes for food as well. You're completely naked, just as your name implies.

speaker: Snake
en: Great. Now I see why you asked me if I like snakes. I suppose calling me "snake" was your idea of a joke, too?

speaker: Tom
en: No, there's a good reason for that. I'll tell you later, when the time is right.

speaker: Snake
en: Gotcha. Getting back to the subject, how exactly am I supposed to feed myself?

speaker: Tom
en: You've been issued a knife and a tranquilizer gun. Use them to hunt for food. You'll also find some medical supplies in your backpack.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, about the backpack... I lost it in a tree on the way down.

speaker: Tom
en: I see. Well, you'd better go back and get it, then. Do you know where it is?

speaker: Snake
en: No problem, I can see it from here. It's stuck on a branch.

speaker: Tom
en: To climb a tree, stand in front of a tree that's covered in ivy and press the action button. I'll be monitoring your progress over the radio. We can't risk violating Soviet airspace, but I'll be in the gunship. My frequency is 140.85. I'll give you a CALL if I need to talk to you. If you need to talk to me, use the SEND function. OK, Snake, go get your backpack.

speaker: Tom
en: I see you've retrieved your backpack, Snake. To equip a weapon, it is necessary to take it out of your backpack. In the Survival Viewer, choose "WEAPON" from the "BACKPACK." Your available weapons will be displayed in a window in the upper-left. From that list, choose the weapon you want to equip and press the Enter button. For other equipped items, just do the same thing from "ITEM."

speaker: Snake
en: Got it! Use the Survival Viewer, "BACKPACK."

speaker: Tom
en: Yep, that's right. Survival is fundamental to this mission. After you've been out in the field for a while, your stamina will start to drop. If your stamina gets too low, it'll affect your performance. You won't be able to shoot accurately, for example, or your wounds won't heal as smoothly. Keep an eye on your stamina so you don't run out. To recover lost stamina, you can hunt for local flora and fauna. You can use either your tranquilizer gun or your knife to hunt.

speaker: Snake
en: My only weapon is an Mk22 Hush Puppy tranquilizer gun?

speaker: Tom
en: That's right. It's been fitted with it's own suppressor. However, the suppressor will deteriorate every time you fire. Once its durability reaches zero, the noise suppression effect will be gone. So don't get too trigger happy with it. The suppressor's durability is shown in the icon. Any weapons and equipment beyond what you're carrying now, you'll have to find as you go.

speaker: Snake
en: I have to find my own weapons and equipment? Whose crazy idea was this anyway?

speaker: Tom
en: Solo covert actions are standard FOX operating procedure. You can't leave any traces of your presence. No weapons, equipment, footprints, sweat, or bodily fluids - the same goes for bullets and cartridges, too. Your presence in enemy territory is already a violation of international conventions of warfare. There aren't supposed to be any American soldiers in Russia. It could spark an international incident. You can't let the enemy see you. You can't let the enemy know you're there. This is a stealth mission. You're a ghost, Snake, in every sense of the word. There'll be no rescue if you're captured. The military and the US government will deny any involvement in the affair.

speaker: Snake
en: Then I'll just have to take care of myself, huh.

speaker: Tom
en: I'm afraid so. You've been given a "fake death" pill for that purpose. SIS guidelines stipulate that soldiers on covert ops like this one be issued a potassium cyanide capsule. Tape it to your body so you can take it when you need to.

speaker: Snake
en: How generous of you.

speaker: Tom
en: Use it if you're taken prisoner by the enemy. It'll send you into a state of false death for a short time.

speaker: Snake
en: ...fooling them into thinking I'm really dead. So how do I come back to life again?

speaker: Tom
en: Just take the revival pill.

speaker: Snake
en: You mean that thing they put in my tooth before the mission?

speaker: Tom
en: That's the one. But be careful. If you remain in a state of false death for too long, nothing will be able to bring you back. Remember that.

speaker: Snake
en: I'll keep it in mind. You said this was a solo mission, right?

speaker: Tom
en: Right.

speaker: Snake
en: I guess that means I can't count on any reinforcements.

speaker: Tom
en: Correct. The mission rests entirely in your hands.

speaker: Snake
en: A real one-man army.

speaker: Tom
en: Relax, there's a support team ready to back you up over the radio.

speaker: Snake
en: Who?

speaker: Tom
en: I'll introduce them to you. This time, survival is of the utmost importance. The first member of the support team will be in charge of monitoring your physical condition - acting a medic, so to speak - as well as recording your mission data. She's a member of FOX as well and she's here on the gunship with me.

speaker: Snake
en: "She"?

speaker: Snake
en: Para...Medic?

speaker: Snake
en: Aren't you going to tell me your real name?

speaker: Snake
en: My name, huh... It's John Doe.

speaker: Snake
en: A name means nothing on the battlefield. After a week, no one has a name. What's your name?

speaker: Snake
en: Very funny.

speaker: Tom
en: She's also in charge of recording your mission data. Whenever you want to SAVE, SEND a message over the reserved SAVE frequency, 140.96.

speaker: Snake
en: So saving lets me record my mission data?

speaker: Snake
en: Good to know.

speaker: Tom
en: There's one more person I want to introduce you to, Snake.

speaker: Tom
en: Speaking of snakes, you remember The Boss, don't you? A legendary soldier and your mentor. Actually, it was The Boss that got the DCI's authorization in the first place. She's going to be serving as FOX's mission advisor.

speaker: Snake
en: The Boss is?

speaker: Tom
en: She also helped me plan this mission. She and I were at SAS together.

speaker: Boss
en: Jack, is that you? How many years has it been?

speaker: Snake
en: Boss??

speaker: Boss
en: That's right, it's me.

speaker: Boss
en: Talk to me. Let me hear your voice.

speaker: Snake
en: It's been 5 years, 72 days, and 18 hours.

speaker: Boss
en: You've lost weight.

speaker: Snake
en: You can tell just by the sound of my voice?

speaker: Boss
en: Of course I can. I know all about you.

speaker: Snake
en: Really. Well, I don't know anything about you.

speaker: Boss
en: What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Snake
en: ...Why'd you disappear on me all of a sudden?

speaker: Boss
en: I was on a top-secret mission.

speaker: Boss
en: You didn't need me anymore.

speaker: Snake
en: But there were still so many things I wanted you to teach me.

speaker: Boss
en: No. I taught you everything you needed to know about fighting techniques. I taught you all I could. The rest you needed to learn on your own.

speaker: Snake
en: Techniques, sure. But what about how to think like a soldier?

speaker: Boss
en: How to think like a soldier? I can't teach you that. A soldier needs to be strong in spirit, body, and technique - and the only thing you can learn from someone else is technique. In fact, technique doesn't even matter. What's most important is spirit. Spirit and body are like two sides of a single coin. They're the same thing. I can't teach you how to think. You'll just have to figure it out for yourself. Listen to me, Jack. Just because soldiers are on the same side right now doesn't mean they always will be. Having personal feelings about your comrades is one the worst sins you can commit. Politics determine who you face on the battlefield. And politics are a living thing. They change along with the times. Yesterday's good might be tomorrow's evil.

speaker: Snake
en: Is that why you abandoned me?

speaker: Boss
en: No. It had nothing to do with you. I already told you, Jack. I was on a top-secret mission. A soldier has to follow whatever orders he's given. It's not his place to question why. But you're looking for a reason to fight. You're a natural born fighter, but you're not quite a soldier. A solider is a political tool, nothing more. That's doubly true if he's a career soldier. Right and wrong have no place in his mission. He has no enemies and no friends. Only the mission. You follow the orders you're given. That's what being a soldier is all about.

speaker: Snake
en: I do whatever I have to do to get the job done. I don't think about politics.

speaker: Boss
en: That's not the same thing. Sooner or later, your conscience is going to bother you. In the end, you have to choose whether you're going to live as a soldier, or just another man with a gun. There's a saying in the Orient; "Loyalty to the end." Do you know what it means?

speaker: Snake
en: Being... Patriotic?

speaker: Boss
en: It means devoting yourself to your country.

speaker: Snake
en: I follow the President and the top brass. I'm ready to die for them if necessary.

speaker: Boss
en: The President and the top brass won't be there forever. Once their terms are up, others will take their place.

speaker: Snake
en: I follow the will of the leader, no matter who's in charge.

speaker: Boss
en: People aren't the ones who dictate the missions.

speaker: Snake
en: Then who does?

speaker: Boss
en: The times. People's values change over time. And so do the leaders of a country. So there's no such thing as an enemy in absolute terms. The enemies we fight are only in relative terms, constantly changing with the times.

speaker: Boss
en: As long as we have "loyalty to the end," there's no point in believing in anything... even in those we love.

speaker: Snake
en: And that's the way a soldier is supposed to think?

speaker: Boss
en: The only thing we can believe in with absolute certainty is the mission, Jack.

speaker: Snake
en: All right. But do me a favor.

speaker: Boss
en: What is it?

speaker: Snake
en: Call me Snake.

speaker: Boss
en: Snake? Oh, right, your codename is Snake. It suits you well.

speaker: Tom
en: That's right. The legendary unit that The Boss put together during World War II was a snake. The Cobra Unit... a group of heroes that brought the war to an end and saved the world. As long as you've got a legendary hero backing you up, you'll be fine. Isn't that right, Snake?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, I can't think of anyone else I'd rather have with me. Oh, and one more thing, Boss...

speaker: Boss
en: Yes?

speaker: Snake
en: It's good to hear your voice again.

speaker: Boss
en: Same here. After all, who knows if either of us will make it out alive... Snake, you were always best at urban warfare and infiltrating buildings. But this is the jungle. Survival is going to be key. Those CQC techniques I taught you are sure to come in handy.

speaker: Snake
en: CQC - close quarters combat, huh. I've been in the Green Berets for the past few years. I'm probably pretty rusty.

speaker: Boss
en: Not to worry. I'll be here to help you remember. After all, this is your first actual survival mission. I'll be supporting you over the radio.

speaker: Snake
en: Where are you, Boss? Next to the Major?

speaker: Tom
en: The Boss is communicating with us by radio from aboard a Permit-class submarine in the Artic Ocean.

speaker: Boss
en: My frequency is 141.80. Call me if you need my advice on battle technique.

speaker: Snake
en: Gotcha.

speaker: Tom
en: Your mission is to retrieve Dr. Sokolov. Dr. Sokolov is being held in an abandoned factory located to the north of your current position. Avoid heavy combat and don't let anyone see you. Don't forget that this is a stealth mission.

speaker: Boss
en: Snake, try to remember some of the basics of CQC.

speaker: Snake
en: Commencing Virtuous mission... now.

speaker: Snake
en: Major, I've spotted two enemy soldiers.

speaker: Tom
en: They're probably KGB troops sent to guard Sokolov.

speaker: Snakes
en: AK-47's and grenades...

speaker: Tom
en: Snake, your presence in Soviet territory is already a violation of international law. We can't let the Kremlin find out that the CIA and the American government are involved. Contact with the enemy is strictly prohibited. Don't engage them in battle either. This is a stealth mission. Got that?

speaker: Boss
en: The Major is right. The point of this mission is to sneak through the jungle without being seen. The success of the mission depends on how well you use your camouflage. Change your camouflage by selecting "CAMOUFLAGE" from the Survival Viewer. The "UNIFORM" option lets you pick your uniform, while the "FACE" option lets you change your face paint. Choosing camouflage that blends in with your surroundings will help you conceal yourself more effectively. Also, don't forget that anything that moves will stand out in the jungle. If you just stand up and run around like an idiot, you're bound to be spotted. But if you crawl instead, you should be able to sneak by without being noticed. You can see how effective your camouflage is by looking at the Camo Index. The Camo Index shows how well your current camouflage blends in with the surrounding area. The higher the value, the harder you are to spot, and vice versa. The key is to make yourself one with nature. Keep that in mind as you go along, OK?

speaker: Snake
en: Major, I've reached the abandoned factory where Sokolov is supposedly being held. This place is a dump. I can't see Sokolov from here... The security here is pretty tight. There are sentries posted around the perimeter... I wonder how many are inside.

speaker: Tom
en: Your objective - Sokolov - is inside the factory... they should be holding him in a room in the northeast sector.

speaker: Snake
en: The northeast section. Got it.

speaker: Tom
en: Be careful. Your mission is to bring Sokolov back alive. He must not be exposed to any kind of danger. Do not approach Sokolov while in the alert phase.

speaker: Snake
en: Right.

speaker: Tom
en: ...Oh, and one more thing, Snake.

speaker: Snake
en: You mean there's more?

speaker: Tom
en: No... it's just... when you get to Sokolov, I want you to tell him something from me.

speaker: Snake
en: And that is?

speaker: Tom
en: "Sorry for being so late."

speaker: Snake
en: Is that all?

speaker: Tom
en: Yes.

speaker: Snake
en: Understood. Beginning my approach to the target.

speaker: Snake
en: You must be Sokolov.

speaker: Sokolov
en: Are you one of Volgin's men? You'll never get it from me!

speaker: Snake
en: No. I'm a CIA agent. I've come to escort you back to the other side of the Iron Curtain.

speaker: Sokolov
en: You're CIA?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah. I was sent by Major Zero, the man who got you out two years ago.

speaker: Sokolov
en: Zero...

speaker: Snake
en: I have a message from him.

speaker: Sokolov
en: What is it?

speaker: Snake
en: He said to tell you "sorry for being so late."

speaker: Sokolov
en: Did he now?

speaker: Snake
en: What does it mean?

speaker: Sokolov
en: It means he's a man of his word. But we've got no time for this. You have to get me out of here before they arrive.

speaker: Snake
en: Who's "they?"

speaker: Sokolov
en: Colonel Volgin of GRU. You in the West know him as Thunderbolt.

speaker: Snake
en: Thunderbolt?... Never heard of him.

speaker: Sokolov
en: He's a member of the army's extremist faction. A man who seeks to seize control of the motherland. Ever since the Cuban Missile Crisis two years ago, Khrushchev has been pursuing a policy of peaceful coexistence with the West. Despite resistance and criticism from hawks in the army, and the provincial authorities, Khrushchev has managed to suppress the opposition so far. But the failure of his agricultural policies has put him in a precarious position. And on top of that... the tragedy last November.

speaker: Snake
en: President Kennedy's assassination.

speaker: Sokolov
en: Precisely. In a sense, Khrushchev has lost his biggest partner, and his power base is rapidly crumbling away. A certain group is plotting to use this opportunity to seize power by rallying the anti-government forces, overthrowing Khrushchev, and installing Brezhnev and Kosygin in his place. The mastermind behind this plot is Colonel Volgin of the GRU. He has control over another secret weapons research facility much like this one - OKB-812, known as the Granin Design Bureau - and is using it to further his plans. But that is not enough to satisfy him. Now he is plotting to seize the secret weapon I have been developing here and use it as leverage in his bid for power.

speaker: Sokolov
en: The intelligence says that they are going to make their move during the test.

speaker: Snake
en: Then the soldiers outside...

speaker: Sokolov
en: Exactly. They wouldn't need that many men just to keep me inside. Their orders were to prevent Colonel Volgin from capturing me. Even if it meant killing me in the process, or so it would seem. Volgin will come, I'm sure of it. You must get me out of here before then.

speaker: Snake
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Sokolov
en: By the way, your Russian is superb. Where did you learn to speak it?

speaker: Snake
en: From my mentor.

speaker: Sokolov
en: Is that so? America is truly a frightening country.

speaker: Snake
en: Having second thoughts?

speaker: Sokolov
en: No. I have no love for this place. Let's go.

speaker: Snake
en: Major, this is Snake. Sokolov is safe with me. He's doing fine. No injuries.

speaker: Tom
en: Good work, Snake. Now hurry up and get Sokolov to the recovery point! We'll rendezvous with you there.

speaker: Snake
en: Roger.

speaker: Tom
en: What about the sentries?

speaker: Snake
en: I had to kill them... there was no other way. But no one will know we were involved.

speaker: Snake
en: I managed to get past them.

speaker: Snake
en: No one spotted me.

speaker: Tom
en: I see.

speaker: Snake
en: What about The Boss?

speaker: Tom
en: We lost contact with The Boss some time ago.

speaker: Snake
en: What happened?

speaker: Tom
en: It's probably just a weak signal. Just hurry and get Sokolov out of there.

speaker: Soldier
en: Freeze!

speaker: Ocelot
en: So this is the legendary Boss? We meet at last.

speaker: Soldier
en: You... You're from the Ocelot unit of Spetsnaz! What's a GRU soldier doing here?

speaker: Ocelot
en: Soldier?

speaker: Soldier
en: He's the Ocelot commander!

speaker: Ocelot
en: That's Major Ocelot to you. And don't you forget it.

speaker: Soldier
en: Sokolov is ours. Now get out of here.

speaker: Ocelot
en: An ocelot never lets his prey escape.

speaker: Soldier
en: What!?

speaker: Ocelot
en: I can't say it feels good to kill a comrade, even if it is for the GRU.

speaker: Snake
en: Sokolov, take cover.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Hmm... You're not The Boss, are you?

speaker: Sokolov
en: GRU operatives...

speaker: Ocelot
en: What is that stance? That gun?

speaker: Ocelot
en: If you're not The Boss, then die!

speaker: GRU Soldier
en: Major!

speaker: Ocelot
en: Leave him! Shoot the other one!

speaker: Ocelot
en: Impossible...

speaker: Snake
en: You ejected the first bullet by hand, didn't you? I see what you were trying to do. But testing a technique you only heard about in the middle of battle wasn't very smart. You were asking to have your gun jam on you. Besides, I don't think you're cut out for an automatic in the first place. You tend to twist your elbow to absorb the recoil. That's more of a revolver technique.

speaker: Ocelot
en: You filthy American dog!

speaker: Snake
en: But that was some fancy shooting... you're pretty good.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Pretty good...

speaker: Snake
en: Major, do you read me?

speaker: Tom
en: I read you. Snake, are you alright?

speaker: Snake
en: I've run into a few snags. These guys were after Sokolov, too. Apparently, they were taking orders from a GRU colonel named Volgin.

speaker: Tom
en: A GRU colonel?

speaker: Snake
en: Part of an internal Soviet power struggle, according to Sokolov. Something between the KGB and the GRU, between Khrushchev's supporters and Volgin's...

speaker: Tom
en: Sokolov was being guarded by the KGB and hunted by the GRU? Snake, it sounds like this could be even hotter than Cuba.

speaker: Snake
en: I don't like it. Something about this whole thing stinks.

speaker: Tom
en: I agree. You'd better hurry.

speaker: Snake
en: Sokolov ran off by himself, but I'll catch up to him.

speaker: Tom
en: We're counting on you.

speaker: Snake
en: You OK?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Those men were from the Ocelot unit.

speaker: Snake
en: Spetsnaz?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Yes. The best GRU has to offer. They're coming for me. I'm finished!

speaker: Snake
en: Calm down. I'll get you out of here. I promise. And we've got some of the best backup we could ask for.

speaker: Sokolov
en: Look!

speaker: Snake
en: That's what they were making you build?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Yes. The Shagohod - "The Treading Behemoth" - a tank capable of launching nuclear IRBMs.

speaker: Snake
en: It can launch nuclear missiles from that kind of terrain?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Oh yes. And without support from friendly units.

speaker: Snake
en: A nuclear-equipped tank capable of operating solo. Is that thing finished?

speaker: Sokolov
en: No. This is only the end of Phase 1. It won't be truly finished until we complete Phase 2.

speaker: Snake
en: Phase 2?

speaker: Sokolov
en: The weapon's true form. If it is completed and the colonel gets his hands on it, it will mean the end of the Cold War.

speaker: Snake
en: The end of the Cold War?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Yes. And then the age of fear will truly begin...

speaker: Snake
en: A world war?

speaker: Sokolov
en: I had no choice but to cooperate! I didn't want to die. I wanted to see my wife and child again in America... Please, take me to America quickly. They cannot complete it without my help.

speaker: Snake
en: Got it. Let's go!

speaker: Snake
en: Boss?

speaker: Boss
en: Good work, Jack.

speaker: Snake
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Boss
en: Sokolov comes with me.

speaker: Snake
en: Hornets!?

speaker: Boss
en: My friends... let us fight together again!

speaker: Fear
en: I have waited long for this day.

speaker: Pain
en: We will fight with you once more.

speaker: End
en: Welcome back, Boss.

speaker: Boss
en: Now that the five of us are together, it's time we go to the depths of hell itself...

speaker: Boss
en: It's raining blood...

speaker: Boss
en: ...is he crying?

speaker: Volgin
en: Kuwabara, Kuwabara... Ah... What a joyful scene.

speaker: Boss
en: Colonel Volgin...

speaker: Volgin
en: Welcome to my country... and to my unit.

speaker: Snake
en: Boss? What is this?

speaker: Boss
en: I'm defecting to the Soviet Union. Sokolov is a little gift for my new hosts.

speaker: Volgin
en: Recoilless nuclear warheads... these will make a fine gift for me...

speaker: Snake
en: This can't be happening!

speaker: Volgin
en: Who is he? Another one of your disciples? Are we taking him with us?

speaker: Boss
en: No. This is one is still just a child. Too pure for us Cobras. He has not yet found an emotion to carry into battle.

speaker: Snake
en: What are you talking about!?

speaker: Boss
en: Think you can pull the trigger?

speaker: Volgin
en: He's seen my face. We can't let him live. If Khrushchev finds out about this, we're finished. He must die.

speaker: Boss
en: Wait. He's my apprentice. I'll take care of him. Jack, you can't come with us.

speaker: Pain
en: The new blood has been rejected...

speaker: Volgin
en: Are we done here?

speaker: Boss
en: Now... on to Sokolov's research facility.

speaker: Volgin
en: Shagohod is ours!

speaker: Boss
en: Drift away. My place is with them now.

speaker: Tom
en: Snake! Can you hear me?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, just barely...

speaker: Tom
en: Snake, listen to me! You need emergency medical treatment. Can you move? You've got to get those wounds treated. Hang in there! All right, let's get you fixed up... Para-Medic?

speaker: Snake
en: Major? The Boss... she's defected.

speaker: Tom
en: We'll talk about that later. First we've got to get you patched up.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah...

speaker: Tom
en: We're coming to get you now. Just stay where you are... we'll drop a recovery balloon. Can you set it up?

speaker: Volgin
en: Excellent. A great success, thanks to The Boss and her Cobras. I have both Sokolov and the Shagohod.

speaker: Ocelot
en: What are we going to with the girl?

speaker: Volgin
en: Who is she?

speaker: Ocelot
en: Apparently she's Sokolov's woman.

speaker: Volgin
en: She's a nice catch. I'll take her.

speaker: Volgin
en: Not so fast, my dear. A Kiss of Death?

speaker: Ocelot
en: Are you KGB?

speaker: Volgin
en: We might be able to use her. She has spunk.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Shall we take her back to the base?

speaker: Volgin
en: Perhaps we should... we have no further use for Sokolov's research facility.

speaker: Volgin
en: I think it's time I gave this marvelous new toy a try.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Colonel! Even if they are our enemies, they're still our countrymen!

speaker: Volgin
en: But it won't be me that pulled the trigger. It will be our friend, the American defector.

speaker: Ocelot
en: You're going to nuke your fellow Russians!?

speaker: Volgin
en: Remember the Alamo.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Colonel!!!

speaker: Pilot
en: Currently flying over the Arctic Ocean. Altitude 30,000 feet. Approaching Soviet airspace. Arriving at the designated drone launch point. Drone oil pressure and voltage are nominal. Payload oxygen supply is nominal. Power supply to payload antifreeze system shows no problems. No gusts. All systems go for drone detachment.

speaker: Zero
en: Snake, we can't risk a HALO jump this time around. Airspace Security has gotten tighter since we were last here. We can't get as close to the ground as we did during the Virtuous mission. So instead we'll be using one of our newest weapons. Snake, you're being given an honor on par with Alan Shepard. This is our last chance. Show your patriotism. If you fail, you'll be back in a hospital bed again waiting for the firing squad.

speaker: Zero
en: So, how does it feel to be a patient in one of the most advanced ICUs in the world?

speaker: Snake
en: Would you do me a favor and tell the suits about visiting hours? I'll never get better with them assaulting me day and night with their questions.

speaker: Zero
en: Must be part of the top brass' inquiry.

speaker: Snake
en: More like an interrogation. According to them, I'm a traitor and an accomplice to The Boss' defection.

speaker: Zero
en: They're just looking for a scapegoat.

speaker: Snake
en: Does that mean they're after you too?

speaker: Zero
en: Let's just say neither one of us is going to be made a national hero out of this.

speaker: Snake
en: Does this mean FOX is going to die?

speaker: Zero
en: No. This fox is still one step ahead of the hounds. The reason I came to see you today... Jack, it's time for FOX to clear its name.

speaker: Snake
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Zero
en: The situation has changed. We've still got a chance to come out of this one alive.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah? What kind of chance?

speaker: Zero
en: Don't get too excited. Here, have a cigar... it's Cuban. This morning I had a meeting with the CIA.

speaker: Snake
en: They decided when they're going to execute us?

speaker: Zero
en: No. Something even bigger. Yesterday, the White House received an unexpected call.

speaker: Chairman
en: President Johnson?

speaker: Johnson
en: Yes, I hear you Mr. Chairman.

speaker: Zero
en: It was a hotline call from Khrushchev to President Johnson.

speaker: Snake
en: From the head of the Soviet Union?

speaker: Zero
en: That's right.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: A few days ago one of our country's main Design Bureaus, OKB-754, was destroyed in a nuclear explosion. At about the same time our anti-aircraft radar picked up a signature that appeared to come from one of your military aircraft. Does any of this sound familiar to you? In retaliation, I have placed our armed forces on secondary alert. Depending on your response, I may be left with no choice but to order the military to maximum alert and unleash Armageddon. With the help of your predecessor I was able to survive the Cuban incident. But my power is not as great as it once was. If I am to survive this crisis, I must have your full cooperation.

speaker: Johnson
en: I should have contacted you myself. Did you know that one of our soldiers defected to your country a week ago?

speaker: Khrushchev
en: No.

speaker: Johnson
en: So you haven't heard then... The man who arranged the defection was a GRU colonel by the name of Yevgeny Borisovitch Volgin.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: Volgin? Of the extremist faction? Go on. Who was this soldier?

speaker: Johnson
en: Her name is The Boss. She's a living legend. During World War II, she was the one who led us to victory in that war. In Russia, you know her as Voyevoda.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: You mean... THE Boss? The mother of your Special Forces?

speaker: Johnson
en: Yes, that's the one. And she took two miniature nuclear shells along with her.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: The Boss took two miniature nuclear shells?

speaker: Johnson
en: I'm afraid so... I believe they were a gift for her new hosts. The "Davy Crockett" Atomic Battle Group Delivery System was completed two years ago. But serious problems were found with the launcher's range and precision. Although they were mass-produced they've never been deployed in battle.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: But Sokolov's research facility was completely wiped out! The whole area is polluted!

speaker: Johnson
en: I can only offer you my deepest condolences over this terrible tragedy.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: So The Boss with Colonel Volgin's help stole two experimental nuclear shells and took them with her as a gift when she defected. Then, shortly thereafter, Sokolov's design lab, a top-secret military research facility, was destroyed by one of these weapons. Am I right so far?

speaker: Johnson
en: Yes, that's correct.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: And the American government denies any involvement in the affair, is that right as well?

speaker: Johnson
en: That's correct. We were not involved in any way.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: Then what was a US military aircraft doing on our radar screen? It was clearly in violation of our airspace. And yet you say it was not acting under your orders?

speaker: Johnson
en: That's correct.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: You expect me to believe that this was all the work of a single soldier?

speaker: Johnson
en: I don't know what else to tell you.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: The army insists that this is all a ploy on your part.

speaker: Johnson
en: I've said it once and I'll say it again. Our government had nothing to do with it.

speaker: Khrushchev
en: And I would like dearly to believe you. However, I'm afraid my power over the military has weakened since the Cuban incident. I will need some kind of proof that was not the action of the American government. You have one week. You must catch The Boss yourselves and recover the remaining nuclear device. Then, you must find some way to prove your innocence.

speaker: Johnson
en: Prove our innocence?

speaker: Khrushchev
en: Yes. Preferably with something... painful. Prove to me that this is not merely another one of your tricks.

speaker: Johnson
en: The Boss should be close to Colonel Volgin. How about a little coaction?

speaker: Khrushchev
en: I would not expect too much if I were you. The political situation here in unstable. And Colonel Volgin is a member of the Brezhnev faction which seeks to topple my government. One week. You have only one week... and if it is not too much to ask, do something about Volgin as well.

speaker: Johnson
en: What is that supposed to mean?

speaker: Khrushchev
en: Nothing... it means nothing. Call it a modest gentleman's agreement to ensure our continued relationship.

speaker: Johnson
en: What if we can't "prove our innocence?"

speaker: Khrushchev
en: Then I will be unable to restrain the military. I will be ousted and they will seek their revenge.

speaker: Johnson
en: A nuclear attack on the United States?

speaker: Khrushchev
en: I leave the disposal of this situation entirely to your discretion, Mr. President.

speaker: Johnson
en: Disposal, huh...

speaker: Khrushchev
en: If you fail, it will mean the beginning of a new world war.

speaker: Zero
en: To put it simply, in order to avoid a full-scale nuclear conflict, we have to prove that America was not involved in that explosion.

speaker: Snake
en: And eliminating The Boss ourselves will prove America's innocence?

speaker: Zero
en: Right. The higher-ups have decided that you're the only one capable of pulling this off. You were her last apprentice. Screw this one up, and we'll both be six feet under. There's no choice.

speaker: Snake
en: Are the Russians going to be helping us?

speaker: Zero
en: The KGB has promised to lend us one of their communications satellites so that you and I can talk to each other.

speaker: Snake
en: That's it?

speaker: Zero
en: They've also put us in touch with a couple of insiders.

speaker: Snake
en: Insiders?

speaker: Zero
en: There was a defection in September 1960... do you remember it?

speaker: Snake
en: You mean the two NSA code breakers who went over to the Soviet Union?

speaker: Zero
en: Precisely. Since then, they've apparently been training with the KGB for exactly this kind of situation. Their code names are ADAM and EVA. I've been told that ADAM has infiltrated Volgin's ranks.

speaker: Zero
en: We've also arranged for him to provide you with an escape route. You'll need to rendezvous with him when you get there.

speaker: Russian pilot
en: Control unidentified aircraft detected. Altitude 30,000 feet. It's fast! Estimated air speed exceeding Mach 3. Bearing south... I'm about to lose it.

speaker: Snake
en: This is Snake. Do you read?

speaker: Zero
en: Loud and clear. Glad to see you landed safely.

speaker: Snake
en: I got blown pretty far off target.

speaker: Zero
en: Snake, let's go over your mission objectives one more time. Rescue Sokolov. Find out what's happened to the Shagohod - then destroy it. And finally, eliminate The Boss.

speaker: Snake
en: Eliminate The Boss...

speaker: Zero
en: This mission will be code-named "Operation Snake Eater."

speaker: Snake
en: Because I'll be taking on The Boss and her COBRA unit, right?

speaker: Zero
en: Don't forget about Colonel Volgin.

speaker: Snake
en: I'm not a hired killer.

speaker: Zero
en: I know. But that was the Kremlin's demand.

speaker: Snake
en: Demand? You mean it wasn't just a request? What's it to us if the Khrushchev regime is threatened by the colonel and his faction?

speaker: Zero
en: If supporting the current regime helps avoid a nuclear exchange, then that's what we'll do.

speaker: Snake
en: And what are the CIA's demands?

speaker: Zero
en: Our priorities are the rescue of Sokolov and the destruction of the Shagohod.

speaker: Snake
en: Roger that, Major Tom.

speaker: Zero
en: Hold on, Snake.

speaker: Snake
en: What now?

speaker: Zero
en: I'm changing my code name. It turns out "Tom" wasn't the most auspicious choice.

speaker: Snake
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Zero
en: Well, the truth is, when I chose my code name... I picked the wrong one.

speaker: Snake
en: The wrong one?

speaker: Zero
en: Did you ever see the movie "The Great Escape?" It came out last year.

speaker: Snake
en: Must have missed that one.

speaker: Zero
en: Anyway, it's based on a true story about prisoners who escaped from a POW camp in Nazi Germany. The prisoners dig three tunnels as part of their plan. But the Nazis find two of the tunnels before they're finished. The prisoners succeeded in escaping by using the last remaining tunnel. The names of those three tunnels were Dick, Harry, and Tom.

speaker: Snake
en: I get it. You used the name of the tunnel they escaped in as your code name because you thought it would bring you good luck.

speaker: Zero
en: Yes, that's exactly right. At least that was the plan...

speaker: Snake
en: ...But?

speaker: Zero
en: But I got the name wrong. The one they escaped in was Harry. Tom was one of the unlucky tunnels - it was discovered by the Nazis before it was finished. I watched the movie again just to make sure. In fact, I even ordered the actual film from the movie company.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, it doesn't sound like the greatest name to use. So, what should I call you instead?

speaker: Zero
en: Hmm. You know, let's just use Zero, like we've been doing all along.

speaker: Snake
en: All right, then, Major Zero it is. We'll start over from square one.

speaker: Zero
en: From square zero. My frequency is 140.85. Oh, I almost forgot. Para- Medic is with is again on this mission.

speaker: Snake
en: Is this her last chance, too?

speaker: Zero
en: If we fail, she'll have her medical license revoked. It's more or less the same kind of fate... Her frequency is the same as during the Virtuous Mission, 145.73. She'll be recording your mission data, as well, just like last time. That frequency is also the same: 140.96. And there's one more person on your support team. His name is Mr. Sigint. He's an expert on the latest in weapons and equipment technology. You'll be going up against some the world's most advanced weaponry when you infiltrate the research facility. If you have any questions, just ask him. His frequency is 148.41.

speaker: Snake
en: Mr. Sigint. Got it.

speaker: Zero
en: ADAM, your KGB contact, is waiting for you at the abandoned factory up ahead.

speaker: Snake
en: The same factory Sokolov was being held in last week?

speaker: Zero
en: Yes. Meet up with ADAM first. He's cleared the way for you to rescue Sokolov.

speaker: Snake
en: How will I know this ADAM guy when I see him?

speaker: Zero
en: You'll know once you reach the factory. The whole area's been polluted by the fallout from that nuclear blast. No one else would dare come close. The password is... "Who are the Patriots?" and "La-Li-Lu-Le-Lo."

speaker: Snake
en: "La-Li-Lu-Le-Lo." Gotcha.

speaker: Zero
en: You've been equipped with a .45 for this mission. Be careful... it's noisy.

speaker: Snake
en: I thought standard FOX procedure was procure on site weapons acquisition.

speaker: Zero
en: The circumstances are different this time. You're now on an official mission for the United States government. It will be necessary to make your presence known to a certain extent. To the Khrushchev regime at the very least. But remember - this is still a sneaking mission. Snake, if you fail this mission, it will mean an all-out nuclear war. Keep that in mind and proceed with extreme caution.

speaker: Snake
en: Understood. Commencing Operation Snake Eater.

speaker: Boss
en: Looks like death wasn't ready for you yet.

speaker: Snake
en: Boss?

speaker: Boss
en: That arm still hurt?

speaker: Snake
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Boss
en: Go home!

speaker: Boss
en: Go home! GRU and my sons are waiting up ahead. You don't have a prayer of finishing your mission - you're not even armed.

speaker: Snake
en: Boss!!

speaker: Boss
en: I'm not your boss anymore. There's nothing for you here. Go home. Go back to your boss. There's no need to prove that you are virtuous here. This isn't America.

speaker: Boss
en: That should stir things up a bit. You'd better hurry. The Border is 60 miles south of here. You ought to be able to run that far.

speaker: Snake
en: Why'd you defect?

speaker: Boss
en: I didn't. I'm loyal... to the "end." To my purpose. What about you, Jack? What's it going to be? Loyalty to your country, or loyalty to me? Your country, or your mentor? Your mission, or your beliefs? Your duty to your unit? Or your personal feelings? You don't know the truth yet. But sooner or later, you'll have to choose. I don't expect you to forgive me. But you can't defeat me, either. You know me too well. Just look at that bandanna. If you can't put the past behind you, you won't survive long. If we meet again, I'll kill you.

speaker: Boss
en: Now, go home!

speaker: Snake
en: This is Snake. Major Zero?

speaker: Zero
en: I read you, Snake.

speaker: Snake
en: I was ambushed by The Boss.

speaker: Zero
en: You were what!?

speaker: Snake
en: The drone's been shot to hell. It's up in flames.

speaker: Zero
en: That's not good. Enemy scouts are going to come looking for you.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, I know. But what was The Boss doing here in the first place? There's got to be a leak somewhere.

speaker: Zero
en: No, that's impossible. The man The Boss is working with, Colonel Volgin, isn't exactly on speaking terms with Khrushchev.

speaker: Snake
en: I lost my gun... The Boss destroyed it.

speaker: Zero
en: Snake, I know how you're feeling. It's hard for me to believe, too - that a legendary hero like The Boss would go over to the Russians, that she'd double cross us like this... But that's how it is, and if you don't accept it, you'll never be able to beat her.

speaker: Snake
en: That's not the problem. In terms of sheer technique, I'll never be able to beat her. I know that all too well.

speaker: Zero
en: You've got to do it, Snake. She's your enemy and your objective.

speaker: Snake
en: Enemy!? We were together for 10 years. And now you tell me she's my enemy?

speaker: Zero
en: Enough. Hurry to the factory where ADAM is waiting. Scouts have probably already been sent out to investigate the explosion. You've lost your weapon, right? That means you've got no chance of winning in a battle situation. Whatever you do, don't let them see you.

speaker: Woman
en: Sorry I'm late.

speaker: Snake
en: Cut the engine, they'll hear us.

speaker: Woman
en: Are you the agent they sent?

speaker: Snake
en: Are you ADAM? I thought you were supposed to be a man.

speaker: Woman
en: ADAM couldn't make it.

speaker: Snake
en: All right, say the password. Who are the Patriots? Who are the Patriots? Answer me!

speaker: Snake
en: Trapped?

speaker: Woman
en: Get down!

speaker: Woman
en: There... is your answer.

speaker: Eva
en: The name's EVA.

speaker: Snake
en: This wasn't part of the plan. What happened to ADAM?

speaker: Eva
en: What's your code name?

speaker: Snake
en: It's... Snake.

speaker: Eva
en: Snake, huh. Well, I'm EVA... are you here to tempt me?

speaker: Snake
en: What happened to ADAM?

speaker: Eva
en: Colonel Volgin is a very suspicious man. He decided ADAM wasn't the right person for this mission.

speaker: Snake
en: And you were?

speaker: Eva
en: Yes.

speaker: Snake
en: Why?

speaker: Eva
en: Because I can do things he can't.

speaker: Snake
en: I heard you used to be a code breaker for the NSA.

speaker: Eva
en: I was. 4 years ago I defected to the Soviet Union with ADAM.

speaker: Snake
en: Mauser Military... the "Broomhandle."

speaker: Eva
en: It packs quite a punch. Nice to have when you're on a bike.

speaker: Snake
en: You held it sideways, and used the muzzle jump to create a horizontal sweep; that was impressive.

speaker: Eva
en: Bet you've never seen that technique in the West.

speaker: Snake
en: It's imitation, isn't it?

speaker: Eva
en: Yeah. It's a Chinese Type 17 pistol. Around here, even that's hard to come by. Don't worry, though. The one I've got for you is American made.

speaker: Snake
en: .45, huh. Incredible...

speaker: Eva
en: Do you like it?

speaker: Snake
en: The feeding ramp is polished to a mirror sheen. The slide's been reinforced. And the interlock with the frame is tightened for added precision. The sight system is original, too. The thumb safety is extended to make it easier on the finger. A long-type trigger with non-slip grooves. A ring hammer... The base of the trigger guard's been filed down for a higher grip. And not only that, nearly every part of this gun has been expertly crafted and customized. Where'd you get something like this?

speaker: Eva
en: I grabbed it from a Western munitions armory. It probably used to belong to one of your officers... and there are more where that came from. You had this with you, didn't you? Better take this, too.

speaker: Snake
en: What's this?

speaker: Eva
en: A disguise to make you look like a scientist.

speaker: Snake
en: A disguise?

speaker: Eva
en: Yes. You're here to rescue Sokolov, right?

speaker: Snake
en: Sokolov's still safe, then.

speaker: Eva
en: Yes. He's being forced to continue his work on the Shagohod.

speaker: Snake
en: Where?

speaker: Eva
en: At the lab. They've got a whole army of scientists there developing new weapons. Security is tight, but if you disguise yourself as a scientist you might be able to sneak in.

speaker: Snake
en: Can we get Sokolov out of there?

speaker: Eva
en: We'll see, won't we.

speaker: Snake
en: Tell how to get to the lab.

speaker: Eva
en: The safest way in is from the rear. First, you'll have to head north through the jungle. You'll come to a heliport used for shipping materials. Pass the heliport and continue north, and there will be a large crevice. Descend into that area and you'll reach a cave. Move through the cave and you will arrive at a mangrove swamp. After the swamp, there'll be a warehouse. Make your way through the warehouse and you'll come out just south of the lab.

speaker: Snake
en: Got it.

speaker: Eva
en: And just what are you doing there?

speaker: Snake
en: In close range combat, a knife can sometimes be more useful than a gun. By doing this, I'll be able to hold a knife at the same time and still keep the gun steady. That way, I can instantly switch between a gun battle and a knife fight. Right. Let's get going.

speaker: Eva
en: Wait a minute.

speaker: Snake
en: What now?

speaker: Eva
en: You must be tired. Why don't you take a little rest?

speaker: Snake
en: I'll be fine.

speaker: Eva
en: You'll never make it in your condition. It's a jungle out there. There's still an hour before dawn. It's dangerous to be out in the jungle at night without a guide.

speaker: Snake
en: What about you?

speaker: Eva
en: I have to get back. I can't be gone for too long. They'll start to suspect something. Don't worry, I'll keep you updated over the radio.

speaker: Snake
en: That's it?

speaker: Eva
en: My orders are to provide you with information. Nothing more... You look disappointed. All right then... I'll do something special for you. I'll stand watch until dawn. Now be a good boy and lie down. What's the matter?

speaker: Snake
en: I don't know you well enough to trust you.

speaker: Eva
en: How well do you have to know me to trust me?

speaker: Snake
en: I don't know if I can trust anybody.

speaker: Eva
en: Gonna get that?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, OK.

speaker: Eva
en: What's the matter?

speaker: Snake
en: We're surrounded. I see... 4 of them.

speaker: Eva
en: We've got company. It's the Ocelot unit. Let's get out of here. Hurry! Don't forget your gear. Here, give me a hand. We can use this to get to the basement. Dammit! Ocelot! I'll get past them on my bike. I'll call you later.

speaker: Snake
en: Okay, I'll keep them busy. !

speaker: Eva
en: Don't go dying on me now.

speaker: Ocelot
en: I've been waiting for this moment...

speaker: Ocelot
en: That's it! That's the stance! I don't think so! Wha...? A female spy? This bitch is wearing perfume... Stay where you are! I've had enough of your judo!

speaker: Snake
en: I see you've got yourself a single action army.

speaker: Ocelot
en: That's right. There'll be no accidents this time.

speaker: Snake
en: You call that an accident? Well... it wouldn't have happened if you hadn't been showing off.

speaker: Ocelot
en: What did you say!?

speaker: Snake
en: It's a nice gun, I'll give you that. But the engraving gives you no tactical advantage whatsoever. Unless you were planning to auction it off as a collector's item. And you're forgetting one more very basic thing... You don't have what it takes to kill me.

speaker: Ocelot
en: We'll see!! !

speaker: Snake
en: 6 shots...

speaker: Snake
en: That thing only carries 6 shots. The Makarov carries 8. You have to get a feel for how many you have left. This is a high class weapon. It's not meant for shooting people.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Damn! This isn't over yet!

speaker: Snake
en: Don't!

speaker: Eva
en: Why?

speaker: Snake
en: He's still young.

speaker: Eva
en: You'll regret stopping me. Dammit! I've got to get back before he does.

speaker: Eva
en: Snake, are you there?

speaker: Snake
en: Eva?

speaker: Eva
en: Did you miss me?

speaker: Snake
en: Did you make it without any trouble?

speaker: Eva
en: No one saw me.

speaker: Snake
en: So you're back with Volgin?

speaker: Eva
en: In a matter of speaking.

speaker: Snake
en: What about The Boss?

speaker: Eva
en: Yeah, she's here too.

speaker: Snake
en: Better be careful.

speaker: Eva
en: Thanks, I will. The Boss and I get along pretty well, though. I guess we traitors have a lot in common.

speaker: Snake
en: Why would anyone want to defect? Betraying your country like... I... I just don't get it.

speaker: Eva
en: Are you talking about The Boss?

speaker: Snake
en: Why'd you do it? Weren't you born and raised in America?

speaker: Eva
en: Yes, in a small rural town. I never even knew there were other countries, other cultures, other ways of thinking. Until I went to work for the NSA. Then, one day, I'd found I'd lost faith in the things I'd been taking for granted.

speaker: Snake
en: What did you see? What was it that made you want to change sides?

speaker: Eva
en: You wouldn't believe me if I told you.

speaker: Snake
en: Try me.

speaker: Eva
en: I saw the universe.

speaker: Snake
en: The universe?

speaker: Eva
en: Not the actual universe. The universe as the intelligence community sees it. I realized that the gravity in this universe was holding me back. That's all. People and their countries are both changed by the environment. And by the times.

speaker: Snake
en: That sounds like what The Boss was saying.

speaker: Eva
en: There's a world of difference between this country and America. But it's only a difference of position. A difference of perspective. Coming here made me realize something. Half of what I'd been told was a complete and utter lie... the other half was a conveniently constructed lie.

speaker: Snake
en: Where's the truth then?

speaker: Eva
en: It's hidden in the lies.

speaker: Snake
en: Are you lying, too?

speaker: Eva
en: Who knows? I've been trained to make even the most severe falsehood sound like the honest truth. Weren't you?

speaker: Snake
en: No. I... believe because I have to. Even if it is a lie. That's part of my mission.

speaker: Eva
en: I'll have to remember that. If you need to give me a call on the radio, my frequency is 142.52. See ya.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Ah, you're here at last. Looks like The Boss' info was right. Twice now you've made me taste bitter defeat.

speaker: Ocelot
en: I hate to disappoint the Cobras but you're mine now. All of you, leave us! It's just you and me. No one to get in our way. Ocelots are proud creatures. They prefer to hunt alone. 12 shots... This time, I've got 12 shots. Okay... Draw!

speaker: Ocelot
en: Damn! He found us!!

speaker: Ocelot
en: You were lucky. We'll meet again!

speaker: Pain
en: I've caught you at last. We are the sons of The Boss. I am The Pain. I will guide you to a world of anguish beyond your imagination. Let's get started!

speaker: The Pain
en: The pain... the pain... the pain! The pain!!

speaker: Sokolov
en: Get your hands off me! I'm not going anywhere!

speaker: Volgin
en: Really now. How many times must I tell you?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Tanya!

speaker: Volgin
en: Each time you resist, your lover will suffer the consequences. Is that clear?

speaker: Sokolov
en: Volgin...!! Damn you!

speaker: Ocelot
en: Hold it right there, traitor. Let's find out just how lucky you are.

speaker: Ocelot
en: Watch closely.

speaker: Ocelot
en: One of these three guns has a single bullet in it. I'm going to pull the trigger six times in a row. Are you ready?

speaker: Ocelot
en: Looks like your luck hasn't run out yet.

speaker: Boss
en: There's no such thing as luck on the battlefield.

speaker: Boss
en: You'd better stay in line from now on. The Cobras will take care of him.

speaker: Volgin
en: Has the CIA dog been disposed of yet?

speaker: Boss
en: The Pain is dead.

speaker: Volgin
en: What!? He may be a child but he's definitely one of yours! I fear Khrushchev may have a hand in this. We have no time to lose. You must eliminate him before the final test.

speaker: Boss
en: Don't worry. They'll be bale to handle it.

speaker: Boss
en: I'm leaving him to you, The Fear.

speaker: Volgin
en: The old man is always sleeping. Is he all right?

speaker: Boss
en: The End is saving what life he has left in him for battle. Normally, he's dead. But he'll wake up when the time is right. And when he does, it will The End for the boy.

speaker: Volgin
en: Sokolov isn't worth your love. You can entertain me until the rain stops. Kuwabara... Kuwabara...

speaker: Boss
en: The Sorrow? Is that you?

speaker: Granin
en: If you're looking for Sokolov, he's not here anymore.

speaker: Granin
en: Put that thing away. You'll spoil my drink. So, you're the intruder everyone's talking about. Typical capitalist dog - no manners.

speaker: Snake
en: And who are you?

speaker: Granin
en: You mean you've never heard of me? And you call yourself an agent. Very well, then. Aleksandr Leonovitch Granin. A man of some importance if I do say so myself. I am the foremost weapons scientist in the Soviet Union and the head of the glorious Granin Design Bureau. This is the Order of Lenin. It is an honor of the greatest magnitude given along with the title of "hero of socialism," to only the finest workers. It was awarded to me in recognition of my brilliant contributions to society. Since the Great Patriotic War, I have created countless weapons in the service of our great communist society. It was thanks to me that we were able to stamp out the Nazi scum. It was I who created the basic design for the mobile ballistic system you know and fear as SS-1C.

speaker: Snake
en: You're crocked, aren't you?

speaker: Granin
en: I am merely drowning my sorrow. Because of him, I've got nothing to do but sit here and drink this crap.

speaker: Snake
en: Him?

speaker: Granin
en: Sokolov! It's him you're looking for, isn't it? Because of him, I have been stripped of my authority. My research has come to nothing. Look! It is a revolutionary mobile nuclear missile system, a bipedal tank.

speaker: Snake
en: A bipedal tank?

speaker: Granin
en: Yes, a walking tank - a robot! Are you familiar with the theory of the missing link between apes and humans? Well, this technology will be the missing link between infantry and artillery. A kind of metal gear, if you well. And this magnificent metal gear will make a revolutionary step forward in weapons development.

speaker: Snake
en: Metal Gear...

speaker: Granin
en: But I won't be used so easily. No, no crying myself to sleep. For you see, I'm going to send these documents to my friend in the United States.

speaker: Snake
en: What!?

speaker: Granin
en: These bastards will live to regret this. And when they themselves become the targets of my creation, they will know my true greatness. Yes! Sokolov's pathetic Shagohod pales in comparison to my work! What are you going to do with a rocket engine on a tank?

speaker: Snake
en: About Sokolov...

speaker: Granin
en: A tank does not need a rocket! It needs something else. Look at these .

speaker: Snake
en: Nice shoes.

speaker: Granin
en: No. Legs!! Legs that allow it to go anywhere!! Just as when humans learned to walk upright! THAT is the real evolution in weaponry! Don't you agree? But... the fools in charge choose Sokolov.

speaker: Snake
en: And where is Sokolov?

speaker: Granin
en: My project has been terminated. The Philosopher's Legacy has been handed over to him.

speaker: Snake
en: What the hell are you talking about?

speaker: Granin
en: The Philosopher's Legacy. Haven't you heard of the Philosophers? The colonel has inherited their immense legacy. Volgin's father was in charge of the Philosopher's money laundering activities. In the confusion of the war, he somehow ended up with their treasure. And Volgin inherited that treasure illegally. We never need to worry about the military budget. The development costs at our facility are all paid out of the colonel's deep pockets. The weapons born here will be the genes for creating an entirely new form of warfare! The funding for my research came out of that legacy. CAME out of it. Now, my money, my men - all have been diverted to the Shagohod project. Tomorrow they will be conducting the final test. While Sokolov is making the final preparations in the weapons factory, at Volgin's main base, the great fortress of Groznyj Grad, here I am playing host to an enemy spy and drinking myself into a stupor.

speaker: Snake
en: That's where they moved Sokolov?

speaker: Granin
en: Yes.

speaker: Snake
en: And the Shagohod is there, too?

speaker: Granin
en: Of course. Hey! You're not thinking of going to Groznyj Grad? Are you mad? It's an impenetrable fortress!

speaker: Snake
en: I'm sure it is.

speaker: Granin
en: You'll be killed!

speaker: Snake
en: I'll take my chances.

speaker: Granin
en: Wait!

speaker: Snake
en: What?

speaker: Granin
en: Listen to me, you fool! I want to help you.

speaker: Snake
en: Help me?

speaker: Granin
en: To thank you for your compliment.

speaker: Snake
en: What compliment?

speaker: Granin
en: My shoes. Tatyana gave them to me. I wanted to thank you for complimenting me on them. I'll tell you how to get into the fortress. In return, I ask only that you get that idiot out of there and destroy the Shagohod. There is an underground tunnel that runs around the perimeter of the base. You should be able to use it to sneak into the base. Head for the mountains. The entrance to the tunnel is located there. Take this. You passed through a warehouse on your way here, didn't you?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah.

speaker: Granin
en: There should have been a locked door inside of it. Do you remember it?

speaker: Granin
en: This key... will open that door. Beyond that door lies a vast jungle. You climb up into the mountains from the far end of the jungle. Go back to the warehouse. Use the key to open the locked door and head for the mountains. Got it?

speaker: Snake
en: Why are you helping me?

speaker: Granin
en: Unlike Sokolov, the thought of defecting has never once crossed my mind. I love... my country. I love this land. I cannot even imagine living anywhere else. I wish to remain a hero... of the great motherland. I cannot bear the thought of being hounded into a corner and left to waste away. It is already dawn. You must hurry. I will remain here and nurse my troubles for a little longer. To capitalism!

speaker: Fear
en: I am The Fear... That bolt is coated with the venom of the Brazilian Wandering Spider. Soon a most exquisite pain will engulf your entire body. Your limbs will be paralyzed, your lungs cease to draw breath, eventually your heart will stop beating. Ah, but what fun would that be? Not a fitting death at all. The Boss' apprentice... I will give you fear such as you've never experienced before. Come into my web... It is time... for you to feel the fear!

speaker: Fear
en: The fear! The fear!! I see it! The fear!

speaker: Eva
en: Snake, are you there?

speaker: Snake
en: Eva? Where are you?

speaker: Eva
en: In the fortress - in Groznyj Grad. Dr. Sokolov is here, too.

speaker: Snake
en: Is he all right?

speaker: Eva
en: He's fine. Right now he's busy putting the finishing touches on the Shagohod.

speaker: Snake
en: Good. That's means they haven't killed him.

speaker: Eva
en: Not yet anyway. But you better hurry. They've already finished the Phase 2 tests. Once the final preparations are complete, they'll have no more use for him. The colonel won't have any qualms about killing him if he thinks the CIA is closing in.

speaker: Snake
en: Eva, you can't let Sokolov out of your sight.

speaker: Eva
en: I know. Snake, do you know where Groznyj Grad is?

speaker: Snake
en: Granin told me that I should be able to get there from the mountains to the north through an underground tunnel.

speaker: Eva
en: Granin told you?

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah. He even gave me the key to the warehouse.

speaker: Eva
en: Why?

speaker: Snake
en: Because he was drunk, I guess.

speaker: Eva
en: You've got to be kidding.

speaker: Snake
en: Hell if I know.

speaker: Eva
en: Snake, there's one problem with that route.

speaker: Snake
en: What problem?

speaker: Eva
en: The mountain entrance to the underground tunnel that leads to the fortress is sealed. You need a key to get in.

speaker: Snake
en: A key... what about the key Granin gave me?

speaker: Eva
en: That key won't work. But don't worry. I'll figure something out. I have an idea. There are some ruins at the top of the mountains. Meet me there.

speaker: Snake
en: The top of the mountains. Got it.

speaker: Eva
en: Wait. There's something else I've got to tell you.

speaker: Snake
en: Now what?

speaker: Eva
en: I heard that one of the Cobras is waiting for you in the jungle at the foot of the mountains. He's a legendary sniper call The End.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah, I've seen him before. That ridiculously old guy, right?

speaker: Eva
en: Don't underestimate him. He's known as the father of modern sniping.

speaker: Snake
en: Is he alone? No spotter?

speaker: Eva
en: None. He's all by himself. Apparently he doesn't need a spotter.

speaker: Snake
en: You can't be serious.

speaker: Eva
en: The entire forest is on his side.

speaker: Snake
en: The forest...

speaker: Eva
en: Stay alert.

speaker: Snake
en: Yeah. I'd hate to have it be the end for me.

speaker: End
en: I beg of you, grant me the strength to take this final prey. Let me linger in the world just a little longer. I have already slept enough for one lifetime... enough for an eternity. You have my thanks. I have to thank you for waking me. If you hadn't shown up... my sleep... would have been eternal. Do you hear me, Snake? I am The End. I am here to send you to your ultimate fate. You'll make a fine quarry for my final hunt.

speaker: Snake
en: Eva, I found that sniper you were talking about.

speaker: Eva
en: That's The End. He's a legend, known as the "Father of Sniping."

speaker: Snake
en: I've got experience sniping in urban and marine environments.

speaker: Eva
en: What about the forest?

speaker: Snake
en: Never.

speaker: Eva
en: I see... well, that forest is divided into three areas: a river, a plateau, and a clearing. He should be lying in wait for you in one of those places.

speaker: Snake
en: Sounds like this may take a while.

speaker: Eva
en: It'll be a test of endurance. Be careful, though. From what I've heard, The End has an almost supernatural knack for camouflaging himself.

speaker: Snake
en: So whoever moves first, loses... This guys' over a hundred years old, though, so I should have the advantage in terms of stamina.

speaker: Eva
en: I wouldn't be so sure if I were you.

speaker: Snake
en: Why's that?

speaker: Eva
en: I've heard that his body is photosynthetic, like a plant.

speaker: Snake
en: What is he, some kind of monster?

speaker: Eva
en: On top of that, he can speak to the forest, too.

speaker: Snake
en: So in other words, he knows it inside out?

speaker: Eva
en: Uh huh. But he doesn't know you. I'm sure you can beat him.

speaker: Snake
en: Don't worry. I intend to.

speaker: End
en: You disappoint me, young Snake... The moment you close your eyes on the battlefield is the moment you never open them again. That's why I don't sleep here...

speaker: Snake
en: Drop your weapon. Drop your weapon!

speaker: Snake
en: Major, I found The End. He's dead. What the hell happened?

speaker: Zero
en: You mean he kicked the bucket in the middle of a battle?

speaker: Zero
en: Well, Snake, the victory is yours.

speaker: Snake
en: No, I don't think so.

speaker: Zero
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Snake
en: It was his dying wish to fight me. But I disappointed him.

speaker: Zero
en: Snake, listen to yourself. This is a mission. It's not a game; it's not a sport. You think you're competing for the gold at Tokyo or something?

speaker: Snake
en: ...I guess you're right...

speaker: Zero
en: Just focus on completing the mission.

speaker: Snake
en: Yes, sir...

speaker: End
en: Spirits of the forest... I thank you. The Boss would be proud of you. The time has come for a younger generation to rise. I've been wandering for more than a century and now my journey comes to a close. What a splendid way... to end it all. I have no regrets... I can return to the forest at last...

speaker: Eva
en: Well, that was quick.

speaker: Snake
en: You look like you could use some rest.

speaker: Eva
en: I'll be fine. It's just that playing these two roles hasn't left me much time to sleep.

speaker: Snake
en: Where'd you get those cuts?

speaker: Eva
en: The colonel.

speaker: Snake
en: He found out?

speaker: Eva
en: If he knew, I'd be dead already. No, this is his "hobby." He's a sadist. He gets pleasure out of making people suffer. He's scum... Does it look that strange to you?

speaker: Snake
en: No. I'm the same way, scars all over.

speaker: Eva
en: Can I see?

speaker: Snake
en: No. Where'd you get this one?

speaker: Eva
en: I got it after defecting to the Soviet Union.

speaker: Snake
en: I don't think so. It's older than that. Code breaking is a desk job. Where'd you get this kind of scar?

speaker: Eva
en: You really want to know? Well, too bad.

speaker: Eva
en: A girl's got to have some secrets, you know. But enough about that. You've got to get going. The Phase 2 trial of the Shagohod is about to start. And it looks like someone might be coming to spoil the party.

speaker: Snake
en: Khrushchev?

speaker: Eva
en: His forces are on their way here. The colonel is gathering his troops together to meet them. If we don't get a move on the security will be even tighter than it is now. You'll need this key. It unlocks the door to the underground tunnel. Once you're in there, you can follow the tunnel to get inside Groznyj Grad. And take this, too.

speaker: Snake
en: What is it?

speaker: Eva
en: The food of the future. A well-balanced meal for the space age. It's good to eat some real food once in a while. I'll bet if I kissed you, you'd taste like a wild animal.

speaker: Snake
en: Do you know where exactly in Groznyj Grad Sokolov is located?

speaker: Eva
en: He's in the heart of the fortress, the weapons lab. The weapons lab is divided into three wings. There's the east wing which houses the research facilities. Then there's the main wing where the weapons are assembled. That's where the Shagohod is. Finally, there's the west wing which is connected via a passageway to the main building. That's where Sokolov is. To get in, you'll have to enter the main wing from the east wing. Then, go through the passageway on the second floor of the main wing.

speaker: Snake
en: The west wing of the weapons lab. Got it.

speaker: Eva
en: There's just one problem.

speaker: Snake
en: Not again...

speaker: Eva
en: The west wing is protected by the highest level of security. You need to be colonel class to get in.

speaker: Snake
en: Colonel class?

speaker: Eva
en: Here, look at this picture. Major Ivan Raidenovitch Raikov. Pretend you're him.

speaker: Snake
en: How do I do that?

speaker: Eva
en: Steal his clothes. You look similar from behind so they won't know the difference. Your face might be a problem so you'll just have to figure something out. He should be somewhere in the east wing.

speaker: Snake
en: All right. But how am I supposed to escape once I get Sokolov out of there? Command said you're supposed to have something ready for me.

speaker: Eva
en: And I do. There's a lake 30 miles north of here. I hid a WIG there.

speaker: Snake
en: A WIG?

speaker: Eva
en: It's a state-of-art ground effect vehicle.

speaker: Snake
en: A ground effect vehicle. I can't fly one of those!

speaker: Eva
en: That's okay. I happen to be an excellent pilot.

speaker: Snake
en: Taking off from a lake is trickier than it looks. It's not like riding a motorcycle. You've got to be delicate.

speaker: Eva
en: Of course I will. You've seen how good I am with the bike, right?

speaker: Snake
en: Right. You handle the escape, then. I'll head for Groznyj Grad.

speaker: Eva
en: Wait a minute. There's something I wanted to ask you.

speaker: Snake
en: What?

speaker: Eva
en: What's the story between you and The Boss?

speaker: Snake
en: She was like a mother... and my master.

speaker: Eva
en: And your lover?

speaker: Snake
en: It went deeper than that.

speaker: Eva
en: Deeper?

speaker: Snake
en: Half of me belongs to The Boss.

speaker: Eva
en: Do you love her?

speaker: Snake
en: No, nothing like that.

speaker: Eva
en: Do you hate her?

speaker: Snake
en: Does it have to be one or the other - love or hate?

speaker: Eva
en: Between a man and a woman. You bet.

speaker: Snake
en: For ten years, we lived and died together. You couldn't possibly understand.

speaker: Eva
en: And you think you can kill her now? That's your mission, isn't it? Assassinating The Boss.

speaker: Eva
en: Snake, is there anyone you like? Someone special?

speaker: Snake
